title: Should a machine look like a machine at a glance?
question: An abandoned prototype carried a rule that was never written down anywhere: machines are square and ride on treads, living things are round and walk. The bot we actually shipped goes the other way — its sheet is a 4x4 walk cycle in the player's exact layout, so today's bot is a small person-shaped helper that walks the way she does, because its renderer *is* her renderer with the texture swapped. The sprinkler, meanwhile, is plainly an object. Nothing says which of those two is the rule and which is the accident.
why_now: The sprinkler is the first automation the player ever meets and the shoo-bot is the debut candidate right behind it (Q-56), so the first two machines in the game are about to stand in the same field. A look drifts when its pieces are drawn months apart with no rule between them. Deciding costs nothing today; deciding after both are drawn costs a redraw.

options.label: Movement decides it, not machinery
options.detail: Anything that moves under its own power reads as a character — bot included; anything static reads as a built object, as the sprinkler already does. Costs nothing, keeps the shipped sheet, and still gives every future sprite a rule to follow. Bets that attachment to your bots (design/06 §2, and the whole of phase 5) is worth more than appliance-legibility.

options.label: Adopt the prototype's rule: square, on treads
options.detail: The strongest at-a-glance signal that this thing was built rather than born — valuable in a game with no words. Costs a new bot sheet and a new animation, not just a texture: treads don't have a four-frame walk, so the renderer stops being the player's.

options.label: Leave it unruled for now
options.detail: Judge each sprite on its own when it comes. Cheapest today, and honest if the answer really depends on seeing them together — but the sprinkler and the debut bot will be drawn at different times, which is exactly how a look drifts. Write a different cut in the judgment box if neither rule above is the one.
